summary: Cannot run pr-arbiter against Tessera's changes: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY exists anywhere, and pr-arbiter has no entry point that reviews a repo other than itself. Both need a human.
tried: Located ~/Claude/pr-arbiter and read its README 'Running it' section — every documented harness (run_baseline, run_triage, phase2_harness) evaluates its OWN fixed 20-PR corpus, not an arbitrary diff.
eval/review_pr.py looked like the general reviewer but is hardcoded to ROOT = pr-arbiter's own repo and diffs that repo's branch vs main. It is a self-dogfood script.

Checked preconditions: no .venv in pr-arbiter (I could build it), and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the environment and no .env* file at all. CLAUDE.md forbids me creating/modifying .env*, and I have no key regardless.
Checked the spend guard would not block the run (rc=0, allowed) — so the blocker is purely the missing credential plus the missing entry point, not authorization.
options: Provide ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (you create .env yourself) and I build the venv + write a small adapter that feeds Tessera's diff to agents.reviewer + agents.arbiter
Skip pr-arbiter; use /code-review ultra on this branch instead — it is the independent pass and needs no adapter
Run pr-arbiter yourself in its own repo and paste findings back
status: resolved:Option 2 chosen: /code-review ultra instead of pr-arbiter. No key needed, no adapter needed, and it reads cross-file — which matters because both defects the self-review found today (INSERT OR IGNORE whose uniqueness lived in the schema; a hook whose correctness depended on a matcher in settings.json) are invisible to pr-arbiter's per-file, single-file-tuned agents. pr-arbiter remains unrun against Tessera; its lack of an any-repo entry point is a real gap tracked in its own repo, not a Tessera blocker.
